intro: Malaysian culture is a blend of Malay, Chinese, Indian and Borneo traditions, celebrated with open houses and famous street food.

chapters.title: Traditions
text: During festivals like Hari Raya, Chinese New Year and Deepavali, families hold 'open houses' where anyone can drop in to eat. Batik fabric, wau kites and wayang kulit shadow puppets are traditional arts.
Peranakan culture, from early Chinese settlers who married locally, has its own food, clothes and architecture.

chapters.title: Food
text: Nasi lemak (coconut rice with sambal) is the national favourite. Laksa, satay, roti canai and char kway teow are eaten at hawker stalls day and night.

keyTerms.meaning: A festival tradition of welcoming all visitors.
